page.layout: One block of text: an italic verse poem of ten lines at the top, set in a block with indented lines; below it, right of centre, the dateline in roman type; below that, a woodcut ornament (no text). No running head, no margin notes. A faint signature at the lower left.

p.i: Persidiam quod iure refers, discordia monstrat Ora animi sensis pignoribusq; tui. Sed bene. Falco tuis resistens viribus acer Coccysmos placido dissipat ore tuos, Et quibus innocuam Philomelā invadere tentas Artibus, ecce illas eripit ipse tibi. Quod si monstroso tu reclamare boatu Niteris, & suaves non capis hosce sonos: En satis est orare Deum, qui arcere furores Atq; tuos fremitus pectoris, arte potest.

page.notes: Woodcut ornament below the dateline: a mask with scrolls and rings, no text. Faint mirrored show-through of the reverse page is visible in the margins and lower half and has been left out. The signature at the lower left is faint and uncertain. No page number or running head is printed. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout; the verse is set in italic.
